Multilingual Document Intelligence: A Comprehensive Study
Authors: Dr. A. Sharma, Dr. R. Ramanujan, Dr. V. Rao
Affiliation: Edge Computing & Language AI Lab
1. Introduction
Long-document question answering poses severe challenges for offline edge deployments.
In many production environments, access to cloud-based APIs is restricted due to privacy
and compliance regulations. This paper introduces an offline framework for long, heterogeneous
documents across multiple languages including English, Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu.
2. Related Work
Standard dense retrieval pipelines frequently suffer from cross-lingual misalignment and lack of
faithful page-grounded attribution.

3. Experimental Methodology & Architecture
We deployed an offline embedding model combined with a local 3.2 billion parameter language model.
All vector indexing was handled via FAISS IndexFlatIP to ensure normalized cosine similarity.
Key Benchmark Results (Experiment 4B):
- Baseline Dense Retrieval Recall: 64.2%
- Proposed Hybrid Framework Recall: 92.7%
- Net Relative Improvement: 28.5% improvement in retrieval recall over naive dense search.
- Average Inference Latency: 1.4 seconds per query on 16GB CPU architecture.
The experiments were replicated across 500 multi-hop queries.

4. Edge Hardware Deployment & Conclusion
The entire system was benchmarked on standard consumer hardware equipped with 16 GB of RAM
and integrated Intel Iris Xe graphics. Zero cloud APIs were queried during evaluation.
5. Reproducibility & Open Source
The model weights for Qwen 2.5 3B were quantized in Q4_K_M format, requiring exactly 2.0 GB of RAM.
In conclusion, self-verifying local RAG demonstrates high citation fidelity and eliminates hallucinations
on unsupported queries.
